label: Fertile concubines
summary: Whether the number of visibly fertile concubines the character has fits a comparison.
details: Compare it with `>`, `<`, `=` and so on. Vanilla uses it once, compared with `max_number_of_concubines`.

label: Number of knights
summary: Whether the number of knights the character has right now fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla mostly compares it with `max_number_of_knights` (10 of its 14 uses), and otherwise with small numbers like `> 0` or `> 1`.

label: Number of lifestyle traits
summary: Whether the number of lifestyle traits the character has fits a comparison.
details: Compare it with `>`, `<`, `=` and so on. Vanilla uses it once, as `<= 2`.

label: Men-at-arms regiments
summary: Whether the number of men-at-arms regiments the character has fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla mostly writes `>= 1` (5 of 8 uses), and also compares it with `number_of_stationed_maa_regiments` or with `recommended_num_maa_regiments_value`.

label: Opposing personality traits
summary: Whether the character and another character have a given number of opposing personality traits between them.
details: The game's documentation does not spell out how the pairs are counted. Vanilla writes `>= 1` most often, and also `<= 0`, `< 3` and `= 2`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of opposing traits.

label: Opposing traits
summary: Whether the character and another character have a given number of opposing traits between them.
details: The game's documentation does not say whether this counts only personality traits or all kinds, nor how the pairs are counted. Vanilla uses it three times, with `>= 1` or `>= 2`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of opposing traits.

label: Number of personality traits
summary: Whether the number of personality traits the character has fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla mostly compares it with limits such as `personality_trait_limit` or `childhood_personality_trait_gain_limit`, or with plain numbers such as `< 3`.

label: Shared personality traits
summary: Whether the character and another character share a given number of personality traits.
details: Vanilla usually asks for at least one or two shared traits (`>= 1`, `>= 2`).

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of shared traits.
fields.values: a comparison such as `>= 2`, `< 3` or a plain number

label: Number of powerful vassals
summary: Whether the number of powerful vassals the character has fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it to ask whether the character has any (`> 0`, `>= 1`). The input does not say what makes a vassal powerful.

label: Shared sinful traits
summary: Whether two characters share a given number of traits that both of their faiths consider sinful.
details: The game's documentation shows the block form with a `target` and a `value`. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of shared sinful traits.

label: Stationed men-at-arms regiments
summary: Whether the number of stationed men-at-arms regiments the character has fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the input. The game's documentation does not say what stationed means exactly.

label: Number of traits
summary: Whether the number of traits the character has fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not say which kinds of traits are counted. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Shared traits
summary: Whether the character and another character share a given number of traits.
details: Vanilla mostly asks for at least one shared trait (`>= 1`), or for none (`<= 0`).

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of shared traits.
fields.values: a comparison such as `>= 1`, `<= 0` or a plain number

label: Number of tributaries
summary: Whether the number of tributaries the character has fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it to ask whether the character has any (`> 0`).

label: Shared virtue traits
summary: Whether two characters share a given number of traits that both of their faiths consider virtuous.
details: The game's documentation shows the block form with a `target` and a `value`. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of shared virtue traits.

label: Title men-at-arms of type
summary: Whether the character has a given number of men-at-arms regiments of one type among the troops of their controlled title.
details: Vanilla gives the men-at-arms type as `target` (for example `varangian_guards`) and the amount as `value`. The game's documentation shows no usage line, so this follows vanilla's one use.

fields.name: target
fields.values: a men-at-arms type key, such as `varangian_guards`

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of regiments.

label: Obligation level score
summary: Whether the score of a vassal contract obligation level, counted in the vassal's favour, fits a comparison.
details: It runs on a single obligation level of a vassal contract, not on a character. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Opinion of
summary: Whether the character's opinion of another character fits a comparison.
details: Opinion is how much the character likes the target. The value can be negative. You can compare with a number or a named opinion value, or give a range as `{ min max }`. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with `>= 0`, `< 0` or `>= 50`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character whose opinion is being checked against: the one the scoped character has an opinion of.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a comparison such as `>= 0` or `< 0`, a named value such as `low_positive_opinion`, or a range `{ min max }`

label: Or
summary: Whether at least one of the conditions inside is true.
details: It is true as soon as one entry is true. Vanilla uses it to list alternatives, such as several duchies or several focuses.

label: Order worldliness
summary: Whether the worldliness of the holy order fits a comparison.
details: Write it inside a holy order, as in `scope:holy_order = { order_worldliness >= 50 }`. Vanilla does not use it in the input, and the game's documentation does not explain worldliness further.

label: Outbreak intensity
summary: Whether the epidemic's outbreak is of a given intensity.
details: The intensities are `minor`, `major` and `apocalyptic`. Vanilla also compares them with `>=`, `>` and `<`, such as `>= major`.

label: Outbreak start date
summary: Whether the date the epidemic's outbreak began fits a comparison with a date.
details: Compare it with `<`, `>`, `=` and so on against a valid date. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Owns a story
summary: Whether the character owns any story that is still active.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Owns story of type
summary: Whether the character owns a story of the given type.
details: Vanilla gives the story type key, such as `story_cycle_pet_cat` or `story_cycle_harrying_of_the_north`.

label: Legacy track perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has fits a comparison.
details: It runs on a dynasty. The game's documentation says the perks are counted "in the lifestyle" but gives no way to say which one, and vanilla does not use it in the input. The key name suggests dynasty legacy perks, but nothing in the input confirms that.

label: Parents' relatedness
summary: Whether the share of DNA that the character's two parents have in common fits a comparison.
details: The value runs from 0.0 (not related) to 1.0 (identical twins), for example `parent_relatedness > 0.25`. The game looks back a number of generations set in its defines (4 by default, 62 ancestors) to find common ancestors.

label: Has the character
summary: Whether the given character takes part in this participant group of a situation.
details: It runs on a situation participant group. Vanilla gives a character such as `root` or `scope:actor`.

label: Kind of group
summary: Whether the situation participant group is of the given type.
details: Vanilla gives group keys such as `nomad_rulers_capital`, `hegemon_ruler`, `other_rulers` or movement groups like `expansion_movement`.

label: Wars participated in
summary: Whether the number of wars the character has taken part in during their life fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says it works only for living characters. Vanilla uses it once, as `>= 2`.

label: Patrilinear betrothal
summary: Whether the character's betrothal is patrilinear.
details: It is false when the character has no betrothal. Vanilla only checks it as `yes`.

label: Patrilinear marriage
summary: Whether the character's marriage to their spouse is patrilinear.
details: Vanilla only checks it as `yes`. The input does not say what the result is for an unmarried character.

label: Percent enemies killed
summary: Whether the percentage of the enemy's soldiers killed, out of all the enemy's soldiers, fits a comparison.
details: It runs on one side of a battle. The number is a percentage, so `>= 80` means at least 80 percent. Vanilla uses `>= 65` and `>= 75`.

label: Perk points
summary: Whether the number of perk points the character has across all lifestyles combined fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it as `> 0` in all 7 uses. The input does not say whether points already spent on perks are counted.

label: Perk points assigned
summary: Whether the number of perk points the character has assigned across all lifestyles combined fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Perks in Diplomacy
summary: Whether the number of perks in the Diplomacy lifestyle fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says only "this lifestyle" and no scope is given, so it is unclear whose perks are counted. Vanilla uses it once, compared with a script value.

label: Perks in Intrigue
summary: Whether the number of perks in the Intrigue lifestyle fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says only "this lifestyle" and no scope is given, so it is unclear whose perks are counted. Vanilla uses it once, compared with a script value.

label: Perks in Learning
summary: Whether the number of perks in the Learning lifestyle fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says only "this lifestyle" and no scope is given, so it is unclear whose perks are counted. Vanilla uses it once, compared with a script value.

label: Perks in Martial
summary: Whether the number of perks in the Martial lifestyle fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says only "this lifestyle" and no scope is given, so it is unclear whose perks are counted. Vanilla uses it twice, once with a script value and once as `>= 2`.

label: Perks in Stewardship
summary: Whether the number of perks in the Stewardship lifestyle fits a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says only "this lifestyle" and no scope is given, so it is unclear whose perks are counted. Vanilla uses it once, compared with a script value.

label: Perks in tree
summary: Whether the number of perk points the character has assigned to one perk tree fits a comparison.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the input.

fields.name: tree
fields.text: The perk tree to count in.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the number of perks.
